newsitem.title: USA: Varian says recovery slower than expected.
newsitem.headline: Varian says recovery slower than expected.

text.p: Varian Associates Inc Thursday said a business recovery expected for second half 1997 is developing slowly.
"The second-half recovery that we were looking for appears to be arriving a bit later than we'd like," Chief Executive Officer Tracy O'Rourke said in a statement.

"However the substantial sequential improvement in shipments in the Semiconductor Equipment business we retained is encouraging. That operation should continue to enjoy very respectable earnings despite the near-term prospect of continued poor year-to-year sales comparisons.
Varian makes instruments and equipment used in semiconductor manufacturing.
Despite the developments for its semiconductor business, it said the instruments division is turning in strong financial results.

"Our Instruments business is having a much better year in 1997, and we expect that to continue," O'Rourke said. "Results in our Health Care activities have lagged our expectations thus far, but that business is gearing up for a considerably stronger final quarter."
Earlier, Varian reported third quarter earnings of $1.67 a share on $359.9 million in revenue versus $1.07 a share on $417 million in revenue one year earlier.
Third-quarter sales declined 14 percent from the year-ago period, and were down 7 percent after adjusting for the June sale of Varian's Thin Film Systems business unit.
Orders in the instruments business reached a record $143 million in the third quarter. Sales also set a third-quarter record at $133 million. Backlog reached $128 million.
Orders for in the semiconductor group totaled $109 million in the third quarter, down 16 percent from last year. Orders were essentially flat with the year-ago quarter.
